compute_tier: Laptop; API (~USD 10–30) for the LLM arm
dataset_name: NHANES 2017–18 CBC_J, FERTIN_J, FETIB_J; external: Mendeley Yemeni hospital set (n=1,998, CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.17632/dmktk7t677.1)
notes: Restrict external model to shared features (Hb, RBC, Hct, MCV, MCH, WBC, platelets, age, sex); RDW missing in Yemeni set. Adjust for inflammation with NHANES CRP (HSCRP_J). External dataset: https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/dmktk7t677/1
novelty_delta: Source used a private single-centre dataset with no code. Adds a fully open pipeline, external validation in an LMIC hospital population relevant to India's anaemia burden, LLM and TabPFN head-to-head, pathologist check against Mentzer/MCH logic, and decision-curve analysis.
proposed_study: Predicting iron deficiency (low ferritin) from routine CBC: develop on NHANES, externally validate on an open Yemeni hospital dataset; logistic regression, XGBoost and TabPFN vs zero/few-shot LLMs
source_title: Predicting Iron Deficiencies Using Routine Complete Blood Cell Count Parameters: A Machine Learning Approach and Evaluation
study_type: Diagnostic prediction model + external validation; LLM vs ML

dataset_name: MIMIC-IV v2.2 (hosp module incl. labevents)
notes: Use MIMIC-IV v2.2 to match shipped split indices. MIMIC data cannot go to external APIs under the DUA: local open-weight models only. Start credentialing now. Cite ClinicRealm (arXiv 2407.18525).
novelty_delta: ClinicalBench inputs had no lab values. Adding structured routine labs tests whether LLMs use numeric lab data as well as gradient boosting, with a lab-only ablation, calibration and an optional small LoRA fine-tune.
proposed_study: Do routine laboratory values change LLM vs ML performance? Extend ClinicalBench (MIMIC-IV mortality, readmission, length of stay) with admission CBC/biochemistry panels
source_title: ClinicalBench: Can LLMs Beat Traditional ML Models in Clinical Prediction?
study_type: EHR prediction / LLM vs ML (retrospective cohort)

dataset_access: open (repo MIT; confirm HF card licence)
dataset_name: MedHallu (~10k PubMedQA-derived pairs; pqa_labeled 1k)
notes: Hallucinated answers were LLM-generated: state as a limitation. The 1k labelled subset is small enough for full expert review.
novelty_delta: Original used GPT-4o, Llama-3.1, UltraMedical; best hard-item F1 was 0.625. Adds newer small open models, a small-model safety-checker design, a pathology/lab-topic subset with expert error taxonomy, and cost/latency trade-offs.
proposed_study: Can small open-weight models detect medical hallucinations? MedHallu on Gemma 3, MedGemma, Qwen3, Llama, with and without retrieved knowledge, plus a pathologist-annotated lab-medicine subset
source_title: MedHallu: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Detecting Medical Hallucinations in Large Language Models

dataset_name: MedMCQA validation split (4,183 Qs; subject field incl. Pathology, Microbiology, Biochemistry)
notes: Repo is MIT with a Colab notebook. MedMCQA keys are noisy, so the answer-key audit is itself a contribution. Could add repeated-sampling consistency (arXiv 2604.10535).
novelty_delta: Source tested only MedGemma 4B/27B with aggregate accuracy. Adds per-subject pathology/microbiology/biochemistry results, newer open models plus 1–2 frontier APIs, a pathologist error taxonomy, an audit of wrong answer keys in pathology items, and cost per correct answer.
proposed_study: Pathology and lab-medicine slice of MedMCQA (AIIMS/NEET-PG style): prompt sensitivity, answer-order bias and permutation voting across open-weight and frontier models, with a pathologist-built error taxonomy
source_title: When Chain-of-Thought Backfires: Evaluating Prompt Sensitivity in Medical Language Models

dataset_access: open (licence varies per subset; avoid ones with unspecified licence)
dataset_name: Medmarks subsets: MedMCQA, MedCalc-Bench, MedHallu, MEDEC, Med-HALT
notes: Harness (MIT) accepts any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so Ollama plugs in directly. Skip Medbullets, MTSamples, MedConceptsQA (unclear licences).
novelty_delta: Medmarks evaluated 61 models at full precision only. Adds quantisation levels on consumer GPU and CPU laptop for Indian low-resource deployment, with tokens/sec, RAM, cost per 1,000 questions and calibration, restricted to lab-medicine tasks (anion gap, eGFR, corrected calcium via MedCalc-Bench).
proposed_study: Laptop-deployable medical LLMs: accuracy and hallucination cost of 4/8-bit quantisation on a lab-medicine slice of Medmarks (MedMCQA-pathology, MedCalc-Bench, MedHallu, MEDEC)
source_title: Medmarks: A Comprehensive Open-Source LLM Benchmark Suite for Medical Tasks

dataset_access: open (SIPaKMeD for research with citation; verify LBC and BCFC licences)
dataset_name: SIPaKMeD (4,049 cells); Mendeley LBC Cervical Cancer; Body Cavity Fluid Cytology
notes: Code MIT. SIPaKMeD and Bethesda labels differ: the binary/Bethesda mapping needs clinical justification. Use original sources, not Kaggle mirrors.
novelty_delta: Source tested five earlier models within each dataset only. Adds UNI2-h, Virchow2, H-optimus, CONCHv1.5, DinoBloom, MUSK and the first cross-dataset normal-vs-abnormal transfer from conventional Pap to liquid-based cytology.
proposed_study: Cervical cytology foundation models: updated benchmark of 2025–26 models with cross-dataset (conventional Pap → LBC) external validation and few-shot LoRA
source_title: Exploring Foundation Models Fine-Tuning for Cytology Classification (ISBI 2025)

dataset_access: open WSIs and clinical data; feature set CC-BY-NC-ND (gating unclear, verify)
dataset_name: TCGA (BRCA, LUAD/LUSC, GBM/LGG) + CPTAC via precomputed UNI2-h features
notes: Repo academic use only. Few Black/Asian patients: report CIs and power. Race is confounded with site (cf. arXiv 2508.14779). Check third-party feature counts against a small self-extracted sample.
novelty_delta: Original used older encoders and private MGB data for breast and lung tasks. Rebuilds the tasks fully on open TCGA (train) and CPTAC (external) with UNI2-h, reports disparity by race, age and submitting site, and tests whether site-stratified splits shrink apparent bias.
proposed_study: Do newer foundation models reduce demographic performance gaps? Race-, age- and site-stratified audit of UNI2-h MIL on TCGA with CPTAC external validation
source_title: Demographic bias in misdiagnosis by computational pathology models (Nature Medicine 2024)

code_url: None from source; reimplementable. Feature extraction: https://github.com/mahmoodlab/TRIDENT
dataset_access: open (CC BY 4.0; free HF login for bulk download)
dataset_name: PLISM (registered multi-scanner, smartphone and multi-stain tiles; Ochi et al., Sci Data 2024)
notes: Full set ~225 GB: download a subset. Tiles already registered, so no WSI handling. Many FMs are CC-BY-NC-ND and gated (institutional email). Cite prior Owkin/Kaiko PLISM numbers; position on scanner/smartphone and calibration.
novelty_delta: Source's 14-model result used in-house data with no code. Re-running its embedding-stability metrics on public, tile-registered PLISM makes it reproducible, adds newer models (H-optimus-0/1, Virchow2, UNI2-h, OpenMidnight, CONCHv1.5) and a smartphone axis relevant to low-resource Indian settings.
proposed_study: Do pathology foundation models see the scanner or the tissue? Open-data test of embedding stability across scanners and smartphones (PLISM)
source_title: Scanner-Induced Domain Shifts Undermine the Robustness of Pathology Foundation Models

compute_tier: RunPod (~60–120 GPU-h; reduce with fewer stain conditions/models)
dataset_name: CAMELYON16/17
notes: Code Apache-2.0. CAMELYON is ~1 TB: use a RunPod volume near us-west-2. Source reports r=-0.22 in abstract vs -0.28 in results; quote carefully.
novelty_delta: Protocol shown only on colorectal MSI with three models. Tests a second task (nodal metastasis), external multi-centre validation on CAMELYON17, and open-licence models, to check whether 'robustness does not track AUC' holds across tasks.
proposed_study: Stain-robustness of foundation-model MIL classifiers beyond MSI: the CTPLab protocol applied to lymph-node metastasis (CAMELYON16 → CAMELYON17)
source_title: A protocol for evaluating robustness to H&E staining variation in computational pathology models (CVPR 2026)

dataset_access: free registration (HF gated, auto-approved, non-commercial, no redistribution); PBC and Raabin open
dataset_name: WBCBench 2026 (~100k images, 13 classes); PBC (17,092 images, CC BY 4.0); Raabin-WBC
notes: Strong fit for a hematology-focused pathologist: class harmonisation needs expert judgement. PBC and Raabin were in DinoBloom pretraining: declare leakage. 267 WBCBench test labels changed after the challenge. PBC: https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/snkd93bnjr/1
novelty_delta: Challenge entries reported only in-distribution macro-F1. Trains frozen-encoder probes on single-institution WBCBench, tests zero-shot on Spanish and Iranian sets with pathologist-harmonised classes, compares DinoBloom with UNI2-h, H-optimus-0, Virchow2 and DINOv2, and reports degradation curves and calibration.
proposed_study: Hematology vs histopathology vs general foundation models for white-cell classification: cross-dataset validation (WBCBench 2026 → PBC Barcelona → Raabin-WBC) and robustness to image degradation
source_title: WBCBench 2026: A Challenge for Robust White Blood Cell Classification Under Class Imbalance

code_url: None; reimplementable in pandas/R (segmented regression, ruptures)
dataset_name: HHS OCR Breach Portal (500+ individuals)
notes: Fastest route to a paper. Download date-stamped snapshots because rows under investigation change. JAMA page blocked automated access; confirm title/DOI by hand. Triangulate with VCDB (github.com/vz-risk/VCDB).
novelty_delta: Prior study ended in 2024 and was descriptive. Adds 2025–2026 data, formal changepoint/ITS models, entity-type and business-associate breakdown, LLM-assisted ransomware tagging validated on a hand-labelled sample, and the first DPDP-compliance translation for Indian hospitals.
proposed_study: US healthcare breaches 2010–2026 from the HHS OCR portal: interrupted time-series and changepoint analysis of hacking/ransomware, with lessons for India's DPDP breach-notification rules
source_title: JAMA Network Open study on hacking/ransomware healthcare breaches 2010–2024 (title and DOI: verify)

code_url: None; reimplementable (CSAF JSON parsing + NVD REST API)
dataset_name: CISA CSAF advisories (ICSMA subset, ~400) + NVD CVE API + FIRST EPSS + CISA KEV
notes: Builds CVE/CWE/CVSS skills useful for TA cyber prep. Check CSAF coverage of pre-CSAF advisories; fill gaps from cisa.gov by hand. Aggregate analysis only.
novelty_delta: Source analysed only 18 FDA communications qualitatively and listed no CVSS scoring and small sample as limitations. A full ICSMA→CVE-linked dataset with CVSS/EPSS/KEV fills exactly those gaps; add CDSCO and DPDP implications for India.
proposed_study: Medical-device vulnerability landscape 2013–2026: all CISA ICS Medical Advisories linked to NVD CVSS/CWE, EPSS and the KEV catalogue
source_title: Cybersecurity breaches in medical devices: analyzing FDA safety communications in response to patient security concerns

dataset_access: open (free download form; WUSTL-EHMS direct download)
dataset_name: CICIoMT2024 (UNB CIC) + WUSTL-EHMS-2020
notes: Crowded field: only publishable with a clear 'published accuracies are inflated' finding. WUSTL-EHMS features differ from CICIoMT2024, so cross-dataset needs a shared feature subset or re-extraction from pcaps. Second dataset URL: https://research.engineering.wustl.edu/~jain/ehms/index.html
novelty_delta: Most CICIoMT2024 papers report 96–99.5% accuracy on random splits of one dataset. Adds dedup and attack-held-out splits to expose inflation, cross-dataset transfer, measured int8 edge latency, SHAP stability, and DPDP framing for Indian hospital networks.
proposed_study: Leakage-aware cross-dataset evaluation of lightweight, explainable IoMT intrusion detectors (CICIoMT2024 → WUSTL-EHMS-2020 / CICIoT2023), with int8 edge models and SHAP stability
source_title: A Tsetlin Machine-driven Intrusion Detection System for Next-Generation IoMT Security (companion: arXiv:2604.06254)

dataset_name: MPIB v1.2 (9,697 instances; direct and RAG-indirect injection)
notes: Released toolkit is minimal; the LLM-judge pipeline must be rebuilt. Keep the payload registry private and report aggregate metrics only. Possible EMNLP 2026 Findings version (verify).
novelty_delta: Original tested 12 models (4B–72B) without newer small models or quantised variants. Adds Gemma-3/Qwen3/Phi-4-mini/Llama-3.2 in GGUF/AWQ, effect of quantisation on clinical-harm rate, one cheap defence stack, and optional Indian-guideline RAG poisoning set.
proposed_study: Prompt-injection robustness of small, on-prem-deployable medical LLMs (<10B, quantised) on MPIB, with lightweight defences and their false-refusal cost
source_title: MPIB: A Benchmark for Medical Prompt Injection Attacks and Clinical Safety in LLMs

dataset_access: open (Camelyon16 CC0; TCGA open on GDC; some FM weights HF-gated, free registration)
dataset_name: Camelyon16; TCGA-BRCA/RCC/LUNG
notes: Best fit with HistoForge work but storage-heavy (Camelyon16 ~700 GB); start with a subset or one TCGA project. Do not release universal perturbations.
novelty_delta: Original attacked slide-level FMs (CHIEF, PRISM, TITAN): ~0.1% perturbed patches dropped TITAN Camelyon16 accuracy from 98% to 42%. Extends to patch-level FMs (Phikon-v2, H-optimus, UNI2) under ABMIL/CLAM, transferability between FMs, JPEG/stain-normalisation defences, and a pathologist's threat-plausibility view.
proposed_study: Adversarial vulnerability and cheap defences for patch-level pathology foundation models in MIL pipelines (Camelyon16/TCGA), with cross-FM transferability
source_title: The Butterfly Effect in Pathology: Exploring Security in Pathology Foundation Models

code_url: None; reimplementable (LASSO → 14-feature XGBoost, isotonic calibration, SHAP)
dataset_name: MIMIC-IV (AP ICU) + eICU-CRD
notes: Shares PhysioNet credential with the cirrhosis study. No open post-ERCP pancreatitis dataset exists. Frame as independent validation.
novelty_delta: Preprint develops on 28-day mortality but validates on in-hospital mortality. A harmonised-endpoint validation with ML vs BISAP/SOFA, decision curves and open code is a credible rapid paper, and builds a pancreatitis pipeline reusable for the planned post-ERCP pancreatitis study.
proposed_study: Acute pancreatitis ICU mortality: reimplement a MIMIC-IV → eICU XGBoost model with a harmonised endpoint, benchmarked against BISAP, SOFA and a parsimonious logistic score
source_title: Development and external validation of a metabolic-clinical XGBoost model for mortality prediction in acute pancreatitis

dataset_name: MIMIC-IV v3.1 + eICU-CRD v2.0
notes: Reported eICU AUROC 0.777. Crowded topic: novelty rests on the score comparison and open code. Same pipeline can later run on RNT cirrhosis data.
novelty_delta: Independent replication plus the head-to-head with MELD 3.0 and CLIF scores the original lacked; a reduced-variable score usable where lactate/urine output are missing; open SQL/R code as a contribution.
proposed_study: Cirrhosis with sepsis, ICU mortality: independent reimplementation of a 13-variable nomogram on MIMIC-IV, head-to-head with MELD 3.0 and CLIF-C scores in eICU, and a reduced bedside score for Indian ICUs
source_title: Development and validation of a prediction model for in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with cirrhosis and sepsis: a multicentre retrospective cohort study
study_type: Prognostic model external validation + comparison with liver scores

dataset_name: NHANES 2017–Mar 2020 (P_LUX) + NHANES Aug 2021–Aug 2023 (LUX_L elastography + CAP, BIOPRO_L, CBC_L, BMX_L, DEMO_L)
notes: MIT repo with NHANES download script. LLM phenotyping step can be dropped. Use survey weights. Check HBV exclusion: only HEPC_L confirmed for 2021–23.
novelty_delta: Original used only 2017–2020 with no external validation. Adds temporal validation on the 2021–2023 cycle, FIB-4 false-negative rates in non-Hispanic Asian and lean-MASLD subgroups (relevant to South Asians), and a simple formula (FIB-4 + HSI + waist) vs XGBoost with DCA and NRI.
proposed_study: Who FIB-4 misses in MASLD: temporal external validation of a 2017–2020 'FIB-4 Plus' model on NHANES 2021–2023, with an Asian / lean-MASLD subgroup analysis
source_title: Decoding Who FIB-4 Fails: An LLM-Augmented Clinical Phenotyping Study Using NHANES 2017–2020 (APASL STC 2026 oral)

dataset_access: open (treat as CC BY-NC 4.0); TCGA-LIHC open via GDC
dataset_name: HepatoBench (87,301 patches, 7 classes) + TCGA-LIHC WSIs
notes: Dataset licence mismatch (card CC BY vs paper CC BY-NC). Paper says not for diagnosis-focused algorithms: frame as quantification. Fits HistoForge FM benchmarking.
novelty_delta: Paper benchmarked only UNI-v1, Virchow-2 and GigaPath. Adds lighter open encoders (H0-mini, Phikon-v2, UNI2, CONCH v1.5), label-efficiency curves, pathologist per-class error review, and a TCGA-LIHC survival test of tissue fractions.
proposed_study: Liver histology tissue classification: benchmark open pathology foundation models on HepatoBench, then test slide-level tissue composition (fibrosis, necrosis, steatosis) against TCGA-LIHC survival
source_title: A Digital Pathology Resource for Liver Cancer Quantification with Datasets, Benchmarks, and Tools (HepatoBench / HepatoQuant)

dataset_name: PolypGen (6 centres, 1,537 frames with masks, CC BY 4.0)
notes: Repo has no licence: reimplement rather than copy. Check whether the MICCAI MLMI 2026 version fixed the bug; if so, shift to external sets and low-cost colonoscope conditions.
novelty_delta: Authors' own v2 note says the encoder was not properly frozen, so the claims are not fully valid. A transparent, correctly frozen reproduction with zero-shot external sets, newer encoders and failure analysis by polyp size and morphology fills a real gap.
proposed_study: Cross-centre generalisation of polyp segmentation: correctly frozen re-evaluation of DINOv2/v3 key features on PolypGen with zero-shot external testing on Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB
source_title: Unlocking Generalization in Polyp Segmentation with DINO Self-Attention "keys"
